headline: Law gives the VA extra 2024 money to keep paying veterans' disability, pension, and education benefits, and requires reports on budget shortfalls.
what_it_does: This law provides extra money for fiscal year 2024 to the Veterans Benefits Administration's accounts for Compensation and Pensions and for Readjustment Benefits. It requires the VA to tell Congress how it will fix its forecasting, data, and budget assumptions for these accounts. It also requires the VA to report on how money in these accounts is being used for 2024 through 2026. The VA's Inspector General must report on what caused projected funding shortfalls and how to prevent them.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and survivors receiving VA disability compensation or pensions
who_it_affects.how: The extra funding goes to the account that pays these benefits.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans using readjustment benefits such as GI Bill education programs
who_it_affects.how: The extra funding goes to the account that pays these benefits.
The VA must report to Congress on budget forecasting fixes and the status of funds, and its Inspector General must investigate the causes of funding shortfalls.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 20, 2024; the funding applies to fiscal year 2024.
